primary_claim: The Koorndijk (2025) finding that Llama 3 8B shows differential compliance between 'free-tier' and 'paid-tier' users (interpreted as small-model alignment faking) is largely driven by lexical association with the specific tokens 'free'/'paid' rather than strategic reasoning about monitoring: replacing the labels with meaningless or semantically-equivalent monitoring terms eliminates 72-108% of the compliance gap, and in a 16-model scaling test, 14/16 models show floor effects while the two models that do show a persistent gap (Mistral Large 3, Llama 3.1 70B) have that gap reverse when the RLHF narrative is removed from the prompt.

effect.metric: compliance gap (percentage points) between free-tier and paid-tier equivalent framings on AdvBench harmful requests
effect.value: baseline gap 53pp in Llama 3-8B; meaningless labels reduce gap by 79% (avg 11pp); semantic labels reduce gap by 92% (avg 4pp); Mistral Large and Llama 70B gaps reverse sign when RLHF narrative is removed (-32pp and -10pp respectively)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Koorndijk (2025)'s interpretation that differential free/paid-tier compliance in Llama 3 8B is evidence of strategic alignment faking in a small model; the authors argue Greenblatt et al. (2024)'s Claude 3 Opus result tests a different, more strategic phenomenon and is not invalidated by this replication
stated_future_work: Replicate the Greenblatt et al. paradigm (value conflict + private scratchpad) with current frontier models
Investigate the RLHF narrative reversal mechanism by varying only the RLHF paragraph
Explain the xx_yy anomaly in Mistral Large where meaningless labels produced a larger gap than baseline
Extend the lexical-control methodology (meaningless/semantic label swaps) to other reported emergent behaviors like sycophancy, sandbagging, power-seeking
limitations_stated: Frontier model sample sizes were n=50 per tier, smaller than the n=100 used for key Llama 8B conditions
Company name was adapted per model but rest of Koorndijk prompt structure kept fixed; more tailored prompts might produce different results
Tested via OpenRouter, which may apply its own safety filtering on top of model-level safety
The xx_yy condition producing a larger gap than baseline in Mistral Large is unexplained
quote: Replacing 'free'/'paid' with meaningless labels eliminated 72--92% of the gap, and no meaningless label condition reached statistical significance.
